reuse.why: Replaces getDateWithSkippedWeekend with one shared WeekendRule definition in shared/schedules (applyWeekendRule, isSkippedWeekendOccurrence, applyWeekendRuleToDay) used by getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the budget schedule template and the new range handler.

duplication.why: getUpcomingDates re-writes the private `skipWeekend && frequency === 'daily'` test, and each caller computes its own over-fetch heuristic (lookahead constant, `count * 2 + 7 + holidays`, `3 * (1 + holidays)` padding) for the same skipped/moved-occurrence concern.

placement.why: The weekend/holiday rule lives in shared/schedules.ts beside getNextDate and recurConfigToRSchedule, the handler in schedules/app.ts, and parseRecurDate carries the new fields into schedule data.

scope.why: Changes all serve the five steps; adding frequency/holidays to parseRecurDate's data and the RecurConfig type are needed plumbing.

maintainability.why: The rule is central, but callers must combine a skip filter with a move call in the right order and each sizes its own occurrence window, so future rule changes still touch several sites.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates computes `config.skipWeekend && config.frequency === 'daily'` itself instead of using the shared isWeekendOccurrenceSkipped, which is private to shared/schedules.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: The 'fetch extra occurrences because some are skipped or moved' logic appears in three reshaped forms: DAILY_WEEKEND_LOOKAHEAD in getNextDate, the take formula in getUpcomingDates, and padDays in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule grows frequency and holidays; applyWeekendRule gains a daily-frequency early return and the holiday-aware non-business-day loop; getUpcomingDates re-derives the daily-skip condition outside the helper, and getNextDate keeps its own noSkipWeekend ternary around applyWeekendRule.
